headline: Council adopts 1.75 residential tax factor for FY 2027, the maximum split rate allowed.
summary: The chief assessor said the residential tax rate falls to $8.33 per $1,000 of value, and the commercial, industrial, and personal property rate to $17.44. Average single-family bills would rise an estimated $173, the chief assessor said. A stormwater presentation listed $75 million in projects and said a stormwater utility could be adopted by FY28. Council also approved a $425,000 EEA grant for a Bennington Triangle park and a petition for six firefighters' credited service.
decisions: Approved 7-0 a resolution honoring Coach Michael Yameen on his retirement.
Referred to the Personnel Committee a request to reopen two discontinued investigations.
Approved spending $280 to support deaf awareness in Lawrence.
Approved a residential tax factor of 1.75 for FY 2027, 8-0.
Approved spending a $425,000 EEA grant for a park at the Bennington Triangle site.
Approved 7-1 the appointment of Leonardo G. Mirabal to the Lawrence Cultural Council.
Approved the appointment of Cristian M. Martinez to the Lawrence Cultural Council.
Approved 8-0 a petition to let six Lawrence firefighters pay for credited service and add it to their pensions.
Approved ordering a public hearing on handicap parking at 67 Inman Street.
Approved ordering a public hearing on a new assistant director of communication position at the Lawrence Public Library.
Approved a resolution recognizing the American Battle Monuments Commission and honoring Leo G. Arsenault of Lawrence.
discussion: Residential tax factor: Members said using the $13.1 million in unused tax levy capacity would not need a ballot question, and that doing so would set a precedent.

Stormwater master plan: The presentation covered combined sewer flooding and listed $75 million in projects. Members asked that zoning and planning boards get the same information on paved surfaces and drainage.

Police investigations: Public speakers said an investigation into a leaked report and an inquiry into hostile work complaints were both stopped, and asked the council to resume them. The request was referred to the Personnel Committee.

Homeless encampment fire: The fire captain said a tent fire on a Saturday appeared unintentional and that no one was inside. He said the tents were all gone by the meeting, and members asked how often tent fires and medical calls happen.

Firefighter pension credit: Six firefighters would pay to add credited service to their pensions, with two credited 24 months and four 22 months. The petition goes to the mayor and then the state, and the governor would need to sign a law covering only these six.
